x-m-e1-06.title: Wetin be the shape of object inside box?
x-m-e1-06.goal: Every time you get one more clue, narrow down the possible shapes and adjust your first idea to fit the new clue.
x-m-e1-06.material: You wear blindfold and feel object inside box, and you hear clues one after one. Object inside na one of box shape, cylinder shape, or ball shape.
x-m-e1-06.thinking.0: Use clues take narrow down the possible shapes
x-m-e1-06.thinking.1: Correct Your Idea with New Clues
x-m-e1-06.thinking.2: Compare Which Clue Best Sorts di Shapes
x-m-e1-06.prereq.0: Know di Features of Box, Cylinder, and Ball Shapes (Grade 1 level)
x-m-e1-06.s.s1.prompt: Dem go show di clues one by one. Each time, choose wetin you think.
x-m-e1-06.s.s1.hint.0: Write box shape, cylinder shape, and ball shape, then mark di shapes wey fit each clue.
x-m-e1-06.s.s1.hint.1: Think one by one about di shapes wey each clue rule out.
x-m-e1-06.s.s1.st.0.info: Clue 1: When I push am with my hand, e roll and roll.
x-m-e1-06.s.s1.st.0.after: If e dey roll, e unlikely to be box shape. Ball shape and cylinder shape remain.
x-m-e1-06.s.s1.st.0.o.a: Na only ball shape fit be.
x-m-e1-06.s.s1.st.0.r.a: Cylinder shape too dey roll if you lay am on e side and push am. You choose only one possibility too quick.
x-m-e1-06.s.s1.st.0.r.b: Box shape get plenty flat faces, so when you push am, e slide and e hard for am to roll.
x-m-e1-06.s.s1.st.0.o.c: E fit be ball shape or cylinder shape.
x-m-e1-06.s.s1.st.0.r.c: You think of all di shapes wey dey roll.
x-m-e1-06.s.s1.st.0.o.d: You no fit know anything from one clue.
x-m-e1-06.s.s1.st.0.r.d: You fit make box shape less likely. Di clue no useless.
x-m-e1-06.s.s1.st.1.info: Clue 2: I put di object for floor and put book on top am, and di book no fall and remain still.
x-m-e1-06.s.s1.st.1.after: For book to stay on top, di top must flat. Ball shape no get flat part. Cylinder shape don become more likely.
x-m-e1-06.s.s1.st.1.o.a: You still no fit tell ball shape and cylinder shape apart.
x-m-e1-06.s.s1.st.1.r.a: You no use di new clue say di book stay still. On ball, book fit roll fall easily.
x-m-e1-06.s.s1.st.1.r.b: Clue 1 talk say e roll, so box shape no really fit.
x-m-e1-06.s.s1.st.1.r.c: You use di new clue choose shape wey get flat top. You correct your idea.
x-m-e1-06.s.s1.st.2.info: Clue 3: I feel di face wey di book dey on, and e flat and round.
x-m-e1-06.s.s1.st.2.ask: Choose wetin di object inside di box fit be.
x-m-e1-06.s.s1.st.2.after: If e get flat, round face, na cylinder shape. Drink can and tuna can both fit.
x-m-e1-06.s.s1.st.2.r.a: Marble na ball shape, so e no get flat face.
x-m-e1-06.s.s1.st.2.r.b: Na cylinder shape with flat, round top.
x-m-e1-06.s.s1.st.2.r.d: Na cylinder shape with flat, round top.
x-m-e1-06.s.s1.st.2.r.c: Die na box shape, so e faces na squares.
x-m-e1-06.s.s1.reflect: How di possible shapes different when you only know clue 1 and when you know up to clue 2? If your first thought na “only ball shape,” which clue make you change your mind?
x-m-e1-06.s.s2.prompt: For another box get object wey be either box-shaped or cylinder-shaped. If you fit ask only one question while blindfolded, wetin be di best question to tell dem apart?
x-m-e1-06.s.s2.hint.0: Think one box shape and one cylinder shape, then for each question write whether di two shapes go answer di same or different.
x-m-e1-06.s.s2.hint.1: Think whether question wey both shapes answer “yes” fit help you tell dem apart.
x-m-e1-06.s.s2.o.a: Di flat face round or square?
x-m-e1-06.s.s2.r.a: E ask about feature wey di two shapes give different answers for.
x-m-e1-06.s.s2.r.b: Both box shape and cylinder shape get flat faces, so both go answer “yes.” E no fit tell dem apart.
x-m-e1-06.s.s2.r.c: Color no get anything to do with shape, so e no fit tell di shapes apart.
x-m-e1-06.s.s2.o.d: E heavy when you lift am by hand?
x-m-e1-06.s.s2.r.d: Weight no get anything to do with shape.
x-m-e1-06.s.s2.explain: Di flat faces of box shape na squares, and di flat faces of cylinder shape na circles. Good question na one wey di two shapes answer differently. Whether e get flat face go be “yes” for both shapes, so e no fit separate dem.

x-m-e1-07.s.s1.r.c: How thick e be no get anything to do with length.
x-m-e1-07.title: Length wey paper clips and glue sticks measure: which one longer?
x-m-e1-07.goal: Learn say you no fit compare lengths measured with different units by counting alone, and decide di information wey you need to compare dem.
x-m-e1-07.material: Minjun measure pencil length with paper clips and get 5 paper clips. Seoyun measure colored pencil length with glue sticks (stick-shaped glue) and get 3 glue sticks. Dem both lay dem in one line side by side with no gaps. Which one longer, di pencil or colored pencil?
x-m-e1-07.thinking.0: Pick di Information Needed to Compare
x-m-e1-07.thinking.1: Make Cases Wey Fit di Conditions
x-m-e1-07.thinking.2: Correct Claim Wey Use Only Counting
x-m-e1-07.prereq.0: Measure Things Length by Number of Same Unit (Grade 1 level)
x-m-e1-07.s.s1.prompt: Wetin information go make you know which one longer? Choose all wey fit.
x-m-e1-07.s.s1.hint.0: One paper clip get same length as one glue stick? Think am first.
x-m-e1-07.s.s1.hint.1: Think wetin must be same to compare two lengths, then find for di options di information wey go help you know.
x-m-e1-07.s.s1.r.a: Order of measuring no get anything to do with length.
x-m-e1-07.s.s1.o.b: How many paper clips equal 1 glue stick
x-m-e1-07.s.s2.var.p: How many paper clips equal 1 glue stick
x-m-e1-07.s.s1.r.b: Dis information go let you change glue sticks and paper clips to di same unit.
x-m-e1-07.s.s1.o.d: Wetin happen when you put di two objects side by side, line up one end, and compare dem
x-m-e1-07.s.s1.r.d: Dis na direct way to compare without using different units.
x-m-e1-07.s.s1.o.e: Di result of counting again how many times you lay di paper clips and glue sticks
x-m-e1-07.s.s1.r.e: Even if di counts correct, if di units different, you no fit compare lengths with counts alone.
x-m-e1-07.s.s1.explain: Paper clip and glue stick get different lengths, so you no fit compare by looking only at 5 and 3. If you know how many paper clips equal 1 glue stick, you fit compare with same unit; you fit also compare di pencil and colored pencil directly by lining up one end.
x-m-e1-07.s.s2.prompt: Say di length of 1 glue stick na p paper clips. For colored pencil (3 glue sticks) to be longer than pencil (5 paper clips), wetin p fit be? Find 2 different p values. (p na whole number from 1 to 6.)
x-m-e1-07.s.s2.hint.0: When p na 1, find how many paper clips 3 glue sticks equal and compare am with 5.
x-m-e1-07.s.s2.hint.1: Change p to 1, 2, 3 and write for table how many paper clips 3 glue sticks equal.
x-m-e1-07.s.s2.ok.c1: p na whole number from 1 to 6.
x-m-e1-07.s.s2.fail.c1: Abeg write p as whole number from 1 to 6.
x-m-e1-07.s.s2.ok.c2: 3 glue sticks longer than 5 paper clips.
x-m-e1-07.s.s2.fail.c2: 3 glue sticks no longer than 5 paper clips. Count how many paper clips equal 3 glue sticks.
x-m-e1-07.s.s2.explain: If p na 2, 3 glue sticks na 6 paper clips, wey longer than 5. If p na 1, na 3 paper clips, so di pencil longer. Di result change according to di length of 1 glue stick.
x-m-e1-07.s.s3.prompt: Minjun talk say, “5 pass 3, so my pencil longer!” Wetin be correct way to think about Minjun claim?
x-m-e1-07.s.s3.hint.0: With di p values you find earlier, find di cases wey Minjun claim correct and di cases wey e wrong.
x-m-e1-07.s.s3.hint.1: Think wetin must be same so di side with bigger count go always longer.
x-m-e1-07.s.s3.o.a: Correct. Di side with bigger count longer.
x-m-e1-07.s.s3.r.a: Na only when di unit same di side with more go be longer. Remember wetin happen earlier when p na 2.
x-m-e1-07.s.s3.o.b: No. Di side wey dem measure with glue sticks always longer.
x-m-e1-07.s.s3.r.b: If 1 glue stick equal 1 paper clip, 3 glue sticks na 3 paper clips, so e shorter.
x-m-e1-07.s.s3.o.c: Di units different, so you need know di length of 1.
x-m-e1-07.s.s3.r.c: You think about how with different units you no fit compare with counts alone.
x-m-e1-07.s.s3.explain: Paper clip and glue stick get different lengths, so you no fit compare with counts alone. Depending on how many paper clips equal 1 glue stick, di pencil fit longer or di colored pencil fit longer.

x-m-e1-09.title: Which Bead Come Next? Guess di Pattern and Correct Am
x-m-e1-09.goal: Learn say with small data you fit read pattern in different ways, and correct your idea about di pattern each time more data come.
x-m-e1-09.material: Dem string apple-shaped beads and grape-shaped beads for necklace with one pattern. I go show you di beads one by one from left.
x-m-e1-09.thinking.0: Think di Possible Patterns from Small Data
x-m-e1-09.thinking.1: Correct Your First Idea with New Data
x-m-e1-09.thinking.2: Predict di Next One with di Pattern
x-m-e1-09.prereq.0: Know Shapes or Numbers Wey Repeat (Grade 1 level)
x-m-e1-09.s.s1.prompt: Dem go show di beads one by one. Each time, choose wetin you think.
x-m-e1-09.s.s1.hint.0: Write di beads wey you don see so far in order, then group and mark di part wey dey repeat.
x-m-e1-09.s.s1.hint.1: Rebuild di earlier beads with di pattern you think of, then check say e match wetin you see.
x-m-e1-09.s.s1.st.0.info: Di first three na apple, grape, apple.
x-m-e1-09.s.s1.st.0.after: With only three, both pattern wey dey alternate and pattern wey repeat every three fit work. You need see more to decide.
x-m-e1-09.s.s1.st.0.o.a: Na grape. I think apple and grape dey come one after di other.
x-m-e1-09.s.s1.st.0.r.a: You find di alternating pattern. Think whether other patterns fit work too.
x-m-e1-09.s.s1.st.0.o.b: Na apple. I think di three beads apple, grape, apple dey repeat.
x-m-e1-09.s.s1.st.0.r.b: You find di pattern wey repeat every three. Think whether other patterns fit work too.
x-m-e1-09.s.s1.st.0.o.c: I no fit choose one. I need see more.
x-m-e1-09.s.s1.st.0.r.c: You think say small data no pin di pattern down to only one possibility.
x-m-e1-09.s.s1.st.0.o.d: One new strawberry-shaped bead show up.
x-m-e1-09.s.s1.st.0.r.d: So far na only apple and grape dey. No reason to tink say new shape go come out.
x-m-e1-09.s.s1.st.1.info: If you count reach five, dem be apple, grape, apple, apple, grape.
x-m-e1-09.s.s1.st.1.ask: Wetin you tink about the pattern now?
x-m-e1-09.s.s1.st.1.after: If e dey take turns, number four for be grape. The pattern wey repeat every three fit am better.
x-m-e1-09.s.s1.st.1.r.a: If you see apple, grape, apple dey repeat, pattern dey.
x-m-e1-09.s.s1.st.1.o.b: The pattern wey dey take turns correct; na only number four happen to different.
x-m-e1-09.s.s1.st.1.r.b: If dem dey take turns, number four for don be grape. You need change your first idea after you see the new information.
x-m-e1-09.s.s1.st.1.o.c: E fit be pattern wey the three beads apple, grape, apple dey repeat.
x-m-e1-09.s.s1.st.1.r.c: You change your idea to match the new information.
x-m-e1-09.s.s1.st.2.info: If you count reach nine, dem be apple, grape, apple, apple, grape, apple, apple, grape, apple.
x-m-e1-09.s.s1.st.2.ask: Wetin the tenth bead go be?
x-m-e1-09.s.s1.st.2.after: The rule wey apple, grape, apple dey repeat every three fit best, so the tenth one na apple. But we no fit sure say no other rule dey at all until more marbles come out.
x-m-e1-09.s.s1.st.2.r.a: Grape dey for places 2nd, 5th, and 8th. Dem dey skip three each time. The next grape go dey 11th.
x-m-e1-09.s.s1.st.2.r.b: You find the first place for the new beginning of the pattern wey dey repeat every three.
x-m-e1-09.s.s1.st.2.o.c: Apple and grape both fit be. Since na only nine we get, other rules still fit dey.
x-m-e1-09.s.s1.st.2.r.c: Na careful thinking to see say other rules fit still dey with nine. If you choose the rule wey fit best, the tenth one na apple.
x-m-e1-09.s.s1.reflect: How your idea about the pattern change between when you see only three and when you see nine? Wetin improve as you see more beads?
x-m-e1-09.s.s2.prompt: One friend talk say, "You fit know the pattern by looking only the first three. You no need look the rest." Wetin be the correct way to tink about this?
x-m-e1-09.s.s2.hint.0: Remember whether the fourth bead don settle as only one thing when you see just the first three.
x-m-e1-09.s.s2.hint.1: Count how many patterns fit dey and how many remain as the information increase.
x-m-e1-09.s.s2.o.a: Correct. If na apple, grape, apple, na rule of taking turns, so no need look further.
x-m-e1-09.s.s2.r.a: If three plenty to choose one rule, you for don know the fourth from the first apple, grape, apple.
x-m-e1-09.s.s2.o.b: No. You no fit know the rule until you see all ten.
x-m-e1-09.s.s2.r.b: How many you need see no get fixed number. Before, five plenty to narrow am down to one.
x-m-e1-09.s.s2.o.c: With only three, you fit read the rule in two ways, so you need look more before you decide.
x-m-e1-09.s.s2.r.c: E consider say with small information, several rules fit dey.
x-m-e1-09.s.s2.explain: With only three, pattern wey dey take turns and pattern wey repeat every three both fit. As the information increase, e narrow down to one. How many you need see depend on the information.

x-m-e1-10.title: Making a pattern wey the fourth number na 12
x-m-e1-10.goal: Make your own pattern wey dey increase by the same amount each time, and see say even if one number na the same, several patterns fit dey.
x-m-e1-10.material: Make we do patterns wey join numbers. Start from the first number and keep adding the same amount. For example, 1, 3, 5, 7 start from 1 and dey increase by 2.
x-m-e1-10.thinking.0: Making a pattern wey fit the conditions
x-m-e1-10.thinking.1: Deciding whether one piece of information determine the pattern
x-m-e1-10.prereq.0: Counting numbers in order and finding say dem dey increase by the same amount (Grade 1 level)
x-m-e1-10.s.s1.prompt: Make 2 different patterns wey the fourth number na 12. a na the first number and d na how much e dey increase each time. (Both must be at least 1.)
x-m-e1-10.s.s1.hint.0: First decide how much e dey increase each time, then start from 12 go backward, remove that amount each time, to find the first number.
x-m-e1-10.s.s1.hint.1: Write the numbers you make in order and check say the fourth one na 12.
x-m-e1-10.s.s1.var.d: How much e dey increase each time
x-m-e1-10.s.s1.ok.c1: The first number and how much e dey increase each time correct.
x-m-e1-10.s.s1.fail.c1: Abeg write the first number and how much e dey increase each time as whole numbers of 1 or more.
x-m-e1-10.s.s1.fail.c2: The fourth number no be 12. Start from the first number and add how much e dey increase each time, three times.
x-m-e1-10.s.s1.explain: 6, 8, 10, 12 start from 6 and increase by 2; 3, 6, 9, 12 start from 3 and increase by 3; and 9, 10, 11, 12 start from 9 and increase by 1.
x-m-e1-10.s.s2.prompt: If you only know say "the fourth number na 12," the pattern don settle to one?
x-m-e1-10.s.s2.hint.0: Find the fifth number for each of the two patterns wey you make before.
x-m-e1-10.s.s2.hint.1: Compare whether the fifth numbers for the two patterns na the same.
x-m-e1-10.s.s2.o.a: E don settle to one. If the fourth one na 12, the pattern na the same.
x-m-e1-10.s.s2.o.b: E no settle to one, but all the fifth numbers na the same.
x-m-e1-10.s.s2.r.b: Find the number after 6, 8, 10, 12 and the number after 3, 6, 9, 12, then compare dem.
x-m-e1-10.s.s2.o.c: E no settle to one. Some patterns get different fifth numbers.
x-m-e1-10.s.s2.r.c: You consider say how much each pattern dey increase different, so the next number different too.
x-m-e1-10.s.s2.explain: After 6, 8, 10, 12 na 14; after 3, 6, 9, 12 na 15; after 9, 10, 11, 12 na 13. Even if the fourth number na the same, different patterns get different fifth numbers.
x-m-e1-10.s.s3.prompt: Write the fifth number for each of the two patterns you make, and talk how the two patterns different.
x-m-e1-10.s.s3.hint.0: Find the number wey come after the fourth number for my pattern.
x-m-e1-10.s.s3.hint.1: Compare how much the two patterns dey increase each time.
x-m-e1-10.s.s3.selfAssess.0: You check again say the fifth number wey you write fit the pattern?
x-m-e1-10.s.s3.selfAssess.1: You write clearly how the two patterns different (how much dem dey increase each time)?
x-m-e1-10.s.s3.model.0: After 6, 8, 10, 12 na 14; after 3, 6, 9, 12 na 15. How much dem dey increase different, 2 and 3, so the fifth numbers different.
x-m-e1-10.s.s3.model.1: The first pattern increase by 2, so e become 14; the second increase by 3, so e become 15. So the fifth numbers different.

x-m-e1-01.title: Showing 52 in different ways with bundles and single ones

x-m-e1-01.thinking.0: Finding di part wey solution leave out

x-m-e1-01.s.s2.fail.c1: Abeg write number of bundles and single ones like 0, 1, 2, 3...

x-m-e1-01.s.s2.explain: 5 bundles and 2 single ones, 4 bundles and 12 single ones, 3 bundles and 22 single ones, 2 bundles and 32 single ones. Each time bundle reduce by 1, single ones increase by 10, and total still 52.
x-m-e1-01.s.s2.because.prompt: Write how many more single ones dey when bundle reduce by 1, and talk why total still 52.

x-m-e1-01.s.s2.because.selfAssess.0: For your explanation, e clear how many single ones equal 1 bundle?

x-m-e1-01.s.s2.because.model.0: When bundle reduce by 1, single ones increase by 10. 1 bundle equal 10 single ones, so total still 52.
x-m-e1-01.s.s2.because.model.1: If you break one bundle, you get 10 single ones. So only the shape change; the number stay the same.

x-m-e1-02.s.s2.r.b: Candidates greater than 60 na 67, 68, and 69; only one get 7 single ones.
x-m-e1-02.s.s2.o.c: E get 6 bundles and under 9 single ones.
x-m-e1-02.s.s2.r.c: 67 and 68 remain, so e no narrow down to one.
x-m-e1-02.s.s2.o.d: E greater than 58 and less than 60.
x-m-e1-02.s.s2.r.d: Only one candidate dey inside this range.
x-m-e1-02.s.s2.r.e: Clue 1 don already say this, so candidates no reduce.
x-m-e1-02.s.s2.explain: Candidates na 56, 57, 58, 59, 67, 68, and 69. You fit find by adding one clue and counting candidates wey remain. If single ones na 8, 58 and 68 remain; if e get 6 bundles and under 9 single ones, 67 and 68 remain. If e greater than 60 and single ones na 7, only 67 remain; if e greater than 58 and less than 60, only 59 remain.

x-m-e1-03.title: "E reduce, so I gats subtract"—na so?
x-m-e1-03.goal: Learn say no be only the words "e reduce" go choose equation; choose am by thinking whether you dey find number before or after e reduce.
x-m-e1-03.material: Doyun dey solve this problem: "Some marbles dey. I give 4 to my friend, and 6 remain. How many marbles dey at first?"
x-m-e1-03.thinking.0: Find the wrong reason in one solution
x-m-e1-03.thinking.1: Check backward whether answer match the story
x-m-e1-03.prereq.0: Experience adding and subtracting numbers up to 20 (Grade 1 level)
x-m-e1-03.s.s1.prompt: Choose the wrong line in Doyun solution. (You fit choose one line only.)
x-m-e1-03.s.s1.hint.0: First think whether the marbles at first or marbles wey remain plenty pass.
x-m-e1-03.s.s1.hint.1: Use Doyun answer of 2 marbles and act out the story: if you give away 4, 6 really remain?
x-m-e1-03.s.s1.line.0: Some marbles dey, and when I give away 4, 6 remain.
x-m-e1-03.s.s1.line.1: I give some away, so marbles reduce. So I subtract.
x-m-e1-03.s.s1.explain: Lines 2 and 3 wrong. True say marbles reduce, but this problem ask how many dey before dem reduce, that is, the amount at first, no be amount after. At first must get more than 6 wey remain. If you give away 4 from answer 2 on line 3, you no fit get 6 remain, so e no match story.
x-m-e1-03.s.s2.prompt: Which equation correctly find the marbles at first?
x-m-e1-03.s.s2.hint.0: Try the story backward. If your friend give the 4 back, how many marbles go dey?
x-m-e1-03.s.s2.hint.1: Act the story again using answer of each equation and check whether 6 remain.
x-m-e1-03.s.s2.r.a: Na Doyun equation. Its answer no match the story.
x-m-e1-03.s.s2.r.b: This equation dey treat 10 as if you already know say na amount at first. But amount at first na the unknown.
x-m-e1-03.s.s2.r.c: This equation join the amount wey remain and amount given away to get amount before e reduce.
x-m-e1-03.s.s2.r.d: You add the 4 marbles wey you give away two times. You give 4 only once.
x-m-e1-03.s.s2.explain: If you join the 6 wey remain and 4 wey you give friend, you get marbles before dem reduce. If you give away 4 from 10, 6 remain.
x-m-e1-03.s.s3.prompt: This time, make stories. Some x marbles dey; after I give away y, 6 remain. Make 3 different examples for number at first. (At most 20 marbles at first, and give away at least 1.)
x-m-e1-03.s.s3.hint.0: Choose number of marbles wey you give away, then think how many must dey at first for 6 to remain.
x-m-e1-03.s.s3.hint.1: Read your story aloud and check if 6 really remain.
x-m-e1-03.s.s3.ok.c1: Numbers dey in the right range.
x-m-e1-03.s.s3.fail.c1: Write marbles at first as 20 or less, and marbles given away as 1 or more, like 1, 2, 3...
x-m-e1-03.s.s3.ok.c2: After you give dem away, 6 remain.
x-m-e1-03.s.s3.fail.c2: Marbles wey remain after giving away no be 6. Take away given marbles from the number at first.
x-m-e1-03.s.s3.explain: If 8 dey at first, give 2; if 10, give 4; if 15, give 9, and 6 remain. The more marbles you give away, the more must dey at first.

x-m-e1-04.title: People enter and leave bus, but number of people stay the same
x-m-e1-04.goal: Learn wetin must happen for total to remain the same when something reduce and something increase together, then make such examples yourself.
x-m-e1-04.material: 10 people dey inside bus. At one stop some people come down and some enter. After that, 10 people still dey inside.
x-m-e1-04.thinking.0: Understand changes in a story (reduce and increase)
x-m-e1-04.thinking.1: Make different cases wey fit the conditions
x-m-e1-04.prereq.0: Experience with stories where numbers around 10 increase or reduce (Grade 1 level)
x-m-e1-04.s.s1.prompt: Wetin you fit tell from this story?
x-m-e1-04.s.s1.hint.0: Think separately wetin make number of people inside bus reduce and wetin make am increase.
x-m-e1-04.s.s1.hint.1: For example, if 2 people come down and 5 enter, think whether number go pass or fall below 10.
x-m-e1-04.s.s1.o.a: More people come down than enter.
x-m-e1-04.s.s1.r.a: If more people come down, number inside bus go below 10.
x-m-e1-04.s.s1.o.b: More people enter than come down.
x-m-e1-04.s.s1.r.b: If more people enter, number inside bus go above 10.
x-m-e1-04.s.s1.o.c: Number of people wey come down and enter na the same.
x-m-e1-04.s.s1.r.c: I think e reduce by some amount, then increase by that same amount, so e return to the first number.
x-m-e1-04.s.s1.r.d: Story talk say some people enter. If nobody enter, e no match the story.
x-m-e1-04.s.s1.explain: Number reduce by how many come down and increase by how many enter. If e still na 10, the number wey come down and enter gats be equal.
x-m-e1-04.s.s2.prompt: Make 3 different cases wey fit the story. Write number wey come down, a, and number wey enter, b. (Both gats be at least 1, and number wey come down no pass 10.)
x-m-e1-04.s.s2.hint.0: First choose number of people wey come down, then count how many people dey on bus.
x-m-e1-04.s.s2.hint.1: Then choose number of people wey enter, and check say e back to 10.
x-m-e1-04.s.s2.var.a: Number of people wey come down
x-m-e1-04.s.s2.fail.c1: Write number of people wey come down and enter as at least 1, and number wey come down as 10 or less.
x-m-e1-04.s.s2.fail.c2: Number of people on bus no stay at 10. Count how many reduce and how many increase again.
x-m-e1-04.s.s2.explain: If two numbers same, like 2 come down and 2 enter, or 5 come down and 5 enter, e stay at 10.
x-m-e1-04.s.s2.because.prompt: Explain why number of people on bus stay same when number wey come down and number wey enter same.
x-m-e1-04.s.s2.because.hint.0: Say separately wetin happen on bus because people come down and because people enter.
x-m-e1-04.s.s2.because.hint.1: Choose one number (for example, 3 people) and follow the story.
x-m-e1-04.s.s2.because.selfAssess.0: Your explanation include both wetin make am reduce and wetin make am increase?
x-m-e1-04.s.s2.because.selfAssess.1: You say the number wey reduce and number wey increase same?
x-m-e1-04.s.s2.because.model.0: 3 people come down, so e reduce by 3, but 3 people enter, so e increase again, and it stay the same.
x-m-e1-04.s.s2.because.model.1: The same number of new people come in and sit in seats as people wey come out, so seats fill again. Same number enter as leave, so e stay the same.

x-m-e1-08.thinking.0: Find the wrong reason in one solution
x-m-e1-08.title: If di long hand dey on 6, na “6 minutes” be that?
x-m-e1-08.goal: Learn say di short hand and long hand for clock show different things, and find and correct di wrong part for Minseo time reading.
x-m-e1-08.material: Minseo read one clock. Di short hand dey between 7 and 8, and di long hand point to 6. (No clock picture dey here. For di clock face, 12 dey top and 6 dey bottom.)
x-m-e1-08.prereq.0: Tell di short hand and long hand apart, read o'clock times and half-past times (:30) (Grade 1 level)
x-m-e1-08.s.s1.prompt: Choose di wrong line for how Minseo read di time. (You fit choose only one line.)
x-m-e1-08.s.s1.hint.0: Remember how you read am when di long hand point to 12.
x-m-e1-08.s.s1.hint.1: Think how many minutes pass as long hand go round once, and where 6 dey for that one round.
x-m-e1-08.s.s1.line.0: Di short hand dey between 7 and 8, so 7 o'clock don pass.
x-m-e1-08.s.s1.line.1: Di long hand point to 6, so na 6 minutes.
x-m-e1-08.s.s1.explain: Line 2 wrong. When di long hand point to 6, you read am as 30 minutes, no be 6 minutes. Na when di long hand wey start from 12 don go half round reach 6. Line 3 just follow line 2, so e no correct too. Line 1 correct.
x-m-e1-08.s.s2.prompt: Which one na di corrected time for wetin Minseo read?
x-m-e1-08.s.s2.hint.0: Look di two numbers wey di short hand dey between, and decide which hour don pass.
x-m-e1-08.s.s2.hint.1: Decide how many minutes di place wey long hand point to mean, then match am with di options.
x-m-e1-08.s.s2.r.a: Na di time when short hand dey between 6 and 7.
x-m-e1-08.s.s2.r.b: Na di answer wey Minseo read first.
x-m-e1-08.s.s2.r.d: E read di hour from short hand and minutes from long hand separately.
x-m-e1-08.s.s2.explain: Di short hand dey between 7 and 8, so 7 o'clock don pass; di long hand dey on 6, so na 30 minutes. So di time na 7:30.
x-m-e1-08.s.s3.prompt: Teach Minseo how to read clock. Write wetin di short hand and long hand each show.
x-m-e1-08.s.s3.hint.0: Write separately wetin you read from short hand and wetin you read from long hand.
x-m-e1-08.s.s3.hint.1: You fit use Minseo clock as example, write in order which hand to look first and which one next.
x-m-e1-08.s.s3.selfAssess.0: You write separately wetin short hand and long hand show?
x-m-e1-08.s.s3.selfAssess.1: You write di reason or way why long hand on 6 mean 30 minutes?
x-m-e1-08.s.s3.model.0: Di short hand show which hour e be, and when di long hand point to 6, na 30 minutes. So di time na 7:30.
x-m-e1-08.s.s3.model.1: Read di hour with short hand first, then read di minutes with long hand. If long hand dey on 6, e don go half round, so na 30 minutes.
x-m-e1-08.s.s3.model.2: Read di hour with short hand and minutes with long hand. If long hand dey on 12, na o'clock; if e dey on 6, na half past.

x-m-e1-05.title: Check the claim "If e roll, e get ball shape"
x-m-e1-05.goal: Use features of different objects to check claim "Everything wey roll get ball shape," and fix the claim so e correct.
x-m-e1-05.material: Seojun talk, "Everything wey roll get ball shape. Marble dey roll and soccer ball dey roll!" For room, marble, soccer ball, snack box (box shape), and drink can (cylinder shape) dey. (Can get flat round top and bottom, and curved side all around.)
x-m-e1-05.thinking.1: Choose object wey prove claim wrong
x-m-e1-05.prereq.0: Recognize and name box, cylinder, and ball shapes (Grade 1 level)
x-m-e1-05.s.s1.prompt: How you fit show say Seojun claim wrong?
x-m-e1-05.s.s1.hint.0: Think each of the four objects one by one, and write whether "e roll?" and "e get ball shape?"
x-m-e1-05.s.s1.hint.1: Check wetin you write and find whether any line contradict Seojun statement.
x-m-e1-05.s.s1.r.a: Marble get ball shape, so e no contradict Seojun statement.
x-m-e1-05.s.s1.o.b: Lay drink can on side and roll am
x-m-e1-05.s.s1.r.b: You test the statement by finding object wey roll but no get ball shape.
x-m-e1-05.s.s1.r.c: Soccer ball get ball shape, so e no contradict Seojun statement.
x-m-e1-05.s.s1.r.d: Box hard to roll, so e no contradict claim say things wey roll get ball shape.
x-m-e1-05.s.s1.explain: To show say Seojun claim wrong, you need only one object wey roll but no get ball shape. Can na cylinder shape, and e roll if you lay am on side and push.
x-m-e1-05.s.s2.prompt: Wetin you wan tell Seojun? Use example object to fix the claim and write am correctly.
x-m-e1-05.s.s2.hint.0: First write the name and shape of object you just choose.
x-m-e1-05.s.s2.hint.1: Also write how you make that object roll.
x-m-e1-05.s.s2.selfAssess.0: E clear say the object you give no get ball shape?
x-m-e1-05.s.s2.selfAssess.1: You talk say ball shape no be the only shape wey fit roll?
x-m-e1-05.s.s2.selfAssess.2: You think too how to place am so e fit roll?
x-m-e1-05.s.s2.model.0: No. Drink can na cylinder shape, but if you lay am down and roll am, e roll. No be only ball shapes dey roll.
x-m-e1-05.s.s2.model.1: No be only marble; can too go roll if you lay am down. So not everything wey roll get ball shape.
x-m-e1-05.s.s2.model.2: No be only ball shapes dey roll. Glue bottle or drum too go roll if you lay am on side.
